cohort: 237 postpartum mothers attending 3 primary health care centers in Suez governorate, Egypt, the majority of whom had completed secondary education (58.6%), were housewives (82.3%), and had undergone cesarean section (76.4%).
finding: The prevalence of postpartum depression was 26.6%, and factors significantly associated with high EPDS scores were bad relationship with the husband, having >2 children, unplanned pregnancy, and unhealthy newborn.
